input.task: Sort the inspector's report and read the sorted inventory turnover.

provenance: T-M42-4 / T-M42-11 (PR #57 R10), the verbatim repro: a `press "Shift"` that touches ONLY the main document, asserting a string that exists ONLY inside the iframe's source pane. Before the fix, `check_state`'s `text_visible` read `page_text(page)` — every frame — so the step recorded `postcondition_ok: true` for an action that did nothing, which is the one thing a postcondition exists to make impossible; the run then extracted from the frame and reported `success` on the strength of a no-op's verified state change. Watched red exactly so: `status success` with `trace_postconditions [true, true, null]`. ADR-036's ruling: a postcondition is checked in the document its action touched — a targetless press touched the main document, whose text does not contain the predicate, so the press fails `act`, the stubbed replan then drops the failed action and reads as if it had worked, and the anti-laundering guard ends the run `failure:act` (the same terminal shape as `replan-cannot-launder-noop-action-in-a-frame`, which pins the guard; this case pins the postcondition scope that feeds it).

triage.note: the decoy document is frames-inner.html; the predicate string appears nowhere in the main document
